Note::NlpAccessor::mask_currency¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::mask_currency() const

Preserve The Sentence, Hide The Amount¶

mask_currency() replaces each recognized monetary amount with the text [CUR]. It is useful when the fact that money was discussed matters, but the amount itself must not survive into logs, corpora, prompts, or features. Unlike deletion, masking preserves a visible category marker and usually leaves the sentence grammatically inspectable.

The recognizer accepts these forms:

Form

Recognized examples

Notes

Leading symbol

$12.50, € 20, £9, ¥100

Optional space follows the symbol. $ amounts may end in k, M, or B.

Leading code

CAD 42, CHF1,250.00

The code match is case-insensitive.

Trailing code

30 eur, 99 GBP

One optional space may separate amount and code.

Supported codes are USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF, CNY, and INR. A bare number is deliberately untouched. Use mask_numbers when every numeric span should be hidden, or mask_pii when several categories must be processed in a defined precedence order.

The method recognizes amount syntax; it does not convert currencies, validate locale-specific grouping, or preserve the currency kind. Every match becomes the same [CUR] marker. Existing markers contain no amount syntax, so applying the method again is idempotent.

Shape, Storage, And Cost¶

The receiver must be a Text Note. Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 reject before cell access. The result is a fresh Text Note with exactly the same rank and extents; the receiver is unchanged. Undefined input propagates as undefined, and a defined empty shape remains defined and empty.

Cells are independent. A cheap character precheck bypasses recognition for cells that contain neither digits nor a supported symbol. Work is linear in the text scanned plus the output produced, with one packed output arena.

Example 1: Symbol Amounts¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"$12.50", "€ 20", "£9", "¥100", "$2M"})
        .nlp().mask_currency()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["[CUR]", "[CUR]", "[CUR]", "[CUR]", "[CUR]"]

Example 2: Currency Codes And A Bare Number¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"CAD 42", "30 eur", "CHF1,250.00", "keep 99"})
        .nlp().mask_currency()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["[CUR]", "[CUR]", "[CUR]", "keep 99"]

Example 3: Matrix Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"$1", "a@b.io", "7pm", "#tag"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().mask_currency()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["[CUR]", "a@b.io"], 
  ["7pm", "#tag"]
]

Only the amount changes. Email, time, and hashtag syntax belongs to other maskers and passes through untouched.

Example 4: Empty, Undefined, And Bytes¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{})
                       .nlp().mask_currency();
std::cout << "currency empty dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel() << '\n';
std::cout << "currency undefined=" << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().mask_currency().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"$1"}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1})
      .nlp().mask_currency();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "currency Bytes: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

currency empty dim=1 numel=0
currency undefined=false
currency Bytes: rejected

See Also¶

  • mask_numbers: hide numeric runs without requiring currency syntax.

  • mask_pii: mask all selected sensitive categories in one ordered pass.
